tables.notes: Pizzas, sides and drinks across three categories, whole-cent prices. Two of them (the two pizzas QA will see first) carry photoUpdatedAt so the photo path has data on first load.

Written by scripts/seed.js, not by a YAML file: a Blob seeded from YAML text would store the text rather than an image, so the script generates two small solid-colour PNGs in code and writes them under the matching MenuItem ids with contentType image/png.

A spread across the three queues and both fulfilment kinds. Every line carries {menuItemId, name, priceCents, quantity} so the owner's queue shows a real per-line price. Two of the six carry customerUserId set to the deterministic id of customer1@example.com, so the past-orders page has data; the rest leave it null as guest orders, and one of those belongs to customer2's address as a guest order that must NOT appear in customer1's list.
The single id 'store' row: open for orders, pickup and delivery on, a fee, a short postcode list, both estimates.

accounts.notes: The shop owner. Signs in with the emailed link, or with the admin password in the preview.
A customer account with a password set, and two seeded orders linked to it.
A second customer account with a password set and no linked orders — the one QA uses to prove one customer cannot see another's orders, and that the owner screens refuse a customer.
